record_type_quote: Given the importance of the investigative proposal made by Vichi et al. (2009), a new replication of this procedure was conducted to examine if, despite the differences between the studied groups, the experimental variables manipulated would select collective behaviors (IBCs).

targets.authors: Vichi, C., Andery, M. A. P. A., & Glenn, S. S.
targets.title: A Metacontingency Experiment: The Effects of Contingent Consequences on Patterns of Interlocking Contingencies of Reinforcement.
targets.evidence_quote: Given the importance of the investigative proposal made by Vichi et al. (2009), a new replication of this procedure was conducted to examine if, despite the differences between the studied groups, the experimental variables manipulated would select collective behaviors (IBCs).
targets.outcome_quote: If, as in Vichi et al (2009) and Lopes (2010), the study considers only if successive gains reached the criterion for contingency change, then we can state that the data here obtained replicated the ones from Vichi et al. and disagree with the ones from Lopes, since all groups reached these criteria. In this sense, the contingencies here manipulated established control over collective behaviors, being an experimental analogous to metacontingencies.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly report replication using the original successive-gain criterion. Their additional statistical analysis is qualified as noncomparable because the original did not conduct it; it is not a stated failed comparison with the original.

reasoning: New groups systematically re-test Vichi et al. (2009). Lopes and Martone are earlier replication context rather than assigned targets.
